question: Status epilepticus is operationally defined as a seizure lasting ≥5 minutes, or two or more discrete seizures without a full return to baseline consciousness between them.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The ILAE 2015 operational definition: seizure ≥5 minutes OR ≥2 seizures without recovery between them = status epilepticus. Treatment begins at 5 minutes (t₁). The older 30-minute threshold has been abandoned because most self-terminating seizures resolve within 2–3 minutes; a seizure persisting at 5 minutes requires immediate pharmacological intervention.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is the ILAE 2015 operational definition used to guide clinical decision-making: ≥5 minutes of continuous seizure (time point t₁ — when treatment should begin) OR two or more seizures without inter-ictal recovery. This replaced the older 30-minute threshold for treatment initiation, recognising that a seizure still active at 5 minutes is unlikely to self-terminate.
